# CodeDAC — full app details

> Independent developer of utility apps for Android and Windows. Every app is free to download with an optional Pro upgrade. Official site: https://codedac.com/ — apps are published only on Google Play and the Microsoft Store.

## Clipboard+ (Android)

Never lose a copied item — every text and image in a searchable clipboard history

Clipboard+ is an Android clipboard manager that keeps every text and image you copy in a searchable history, newest first. Since Android 10, no app may read the clipboard in the background, so Clipboard+ saves what you copied the moment it becomes active — when you open the app, tap the floating panel, or use the widget — or right away when you tap Clipboard+ in the text selection menu. Turn on Auto-save (optional) and Clipboard+ uses Android's Accessibility service to save what you copy in other apps the moment you copy it, without opening the app — it can't read other apps' screens and skips passwords. A resizable floating overlay lets you reach your clipboard history from any screen without switching apps. Organize frequently used text into snippets and groups, and paste any clip fast with keyword search, a home screen widget, and a notification panel. You can also export your history to PDF and back up or restore your clips anytime. Pair it with Clipboard+ for Windows and what you copy on your phone pastes on your PC, and what you copy on your PC pastes on your phone. You just sign in to Google Drive with the same account in both apps, and your clips never pass through a CodeDAC server — they are stored only in your own Google Drive.

Features:
- Optional Auto-save keeps what you copy the moment you copy it; text and images in a searchable history, newest first
- Resizable floating overlay for use over any app
- Organize frequent text into snippets and groups
- Instant search and filter by keyword, text, image, or date
- Fast paste from a home screen widget and the notification panel, and save from any app via the text selection menu
- Bidirectional phone-to-PC sync through your own Google Drive, export clipboard history to PDF, plus backup and restore

FAQ:
- Q: When does Clipboard+ save what I copy?
  A: Turn on Auto-save (optional, off by default) and what you copy in other apps is saved the moment you copy it, without opening Clipboard+. It uses Android's Accessibility service only to notice the copy — it can't read other apps' screens, skips clips marked as passwords and sends nothing anywhere. Without it, Android 10+ lets apps read the clipboard only while they're on screen, so Clipboard+ saves when you open the app, tap the floating bubble or use the widget, or when you choose Clipboard+ in the text selection menu.
- Q: Can I access my clipboard history while using other apps?
  A: Yes. A resizable floating overlay lets you reach your history from any screen without switching apps.
- Q: Does it sync with my Windows PC?
  A: Yes. Install Clipboard+ for Windows as well, then in the settings of both apps sign in to Google Drive with the same account and turn on automatic sync. From then on, what you copy on your phone pastes on your PC, and what you copy on your PC pastes on your phone. Your clips never pass through a CodeDAC server — they are stored only in your own Google Drive.
- Q: What is free, and what does Pro add?
  A: Free keeps your text and image clipboard history with search, snippets, up to 3 groups, the floating panel, the widget and the selection-menu shortcut, and it shows ads. Pro removes the ads and adds phone-to-PC sync through your own Google Drive, unlimited image clips, the expanded floating panel and widget, unlimited groups, PDF export and backup restore — monthly, yearly or as a one-time lifetime purchase.

Page: https://codedac.com/apps/clipboard.html
Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.clipboard

## AutoStart+ (Android)

Auto start your apps after every reboot, as soon as you unlock your phone. No root, set once, runs forever.

AutoStart+ is the simplest auto start manager for Android: pick the apps you want and they launch on their own after every reboot, as soon as you unlock the phone — no root, no scripts, no daily tapping. Search every installed app to add it in seconds, switch each one on or off with a tap, and drag the rows to set the order they start in. You don't have to reboot to test it: the ⋮ menu on any row opens that app right away, and after boot a short message tells you what started, with one tap to run the rest. The free version auto starts 1 app; PRO lifts the limit so the whole list launches in order. Most Android car head units go to sleep instead of restarting when you turn off the car. Turn on Car Mode and your apps open again every time the screen wakes after being off for 3+ minutes. Free.

Features:
- Auto starts your selected apps after every reboot, as soon as you unlock the phone — no root, no custom ROM
- Car Mode for head units: your apps open again every time the screen wakes from sleep — free
- Drag the rows to decide which app starts first at every boot
- Launch delay (PRO): wait a few seconds before the first app and space the rest apart, so car head units and slow devices finish starting up first
- Run now from any row's ⋮ menu — check your list without rebooting the phone
- After a reboot, a banner starts your whole list in one tap as soon as you unlock the phone (PRO)
- Free auto starts 1 app; PRO lifts the limit and launches your whole list in order

FAQ:
- Q: My apps don't launch after boot. What should I do?
  A: Xiaomi, OPPO, vivo and Huawei block background startup by default. AutoStart+ recognises your device and takes you straight to the “Autostart” screen in the phone's own security settings — allow it there and boot launching works. Leaving AutoStart+ out of battery optimisation helps too.
- Q: Does AutoStart+ work on Android car head units?
  A: Most Android car head units go to sleep instead of restarting when you turn off the car. Turn on Car Mode and your apps open again every time the screen wakes after being off for 3+ minutes. Free.
- Q: How many apps can I auto start?
  A: The free version starts 1 app per boot. PRO removes the limit, so the whole list launches in the order you set.
- Q: Will it drain my battery?
  A: AutoStart+ runs only once at boot and is not an always-on background app, so it has almost no impact on battery life.
- Q: Is there an official AutoStart+ APK?
  A: No. AutoStart+ is published only on Google Play, and this site is its official website — we don’t release APK files anywhere else. An APK from another site may be modified or out of date, so please install it from Google Play.

Page: https://codedac.com/apps/autostart.html
Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.autostart

## FloatCalc+ (Android)

Calculate without leaving your app — a floating calculator that stays on top.

FloatCalc+ is a floating calculator that stays on top of any app, so you never have to close your shopping, banking or browser screen just to work something out. The calculator, unit converter and currency converter share one draggable window and one familiar keypad, and the result appears as you type. Select a number in any app and tap “Calculate with FloatCalc+” to bring it straight in, or open the panel from the Quick Settings tile, a home screen widget or the notification. Shrink it to an icon at the edge of the screen when you need the space. Exchange rates come from the European Central Bank and refresh daily, cached so everything keeps working offline.

Features:
- Floats over any app — YouTube, maps, browser, banking, shopping, documents — and reopens in the mode you used last
- The usual calculator keypad with a live result as you type; long-press % for ^ and ÷ for √
- Select a number in any app and tap “Calculate with FloatCalc+”; copy and paste from the ⋮ menu, or long-press the result to copy it
- Unit and currency converters on the same keypad: length, weight, temperature, area, volume, speed and time, plus daily ECB rates for 30+ currencies
- Open it from the Quick Settings tile, a home screen widget or the notification buttons
- Shrink the panel to an icon docked at the screen edge, or let it shrink by itself; large keys, key vibration, adjustable opacity and 8 themes, with the default theme following dark mode

FAQ:
- Q: Do I have to close my app every time I want to calculate?
  A: No. FloatCalc+ is a floating window that stays on top of other apps, so you can work out a discount or convert a price without leaving your shopping, banking or browser screen. Select a number in the app and tap “Calculate with FloatCalc+”, or just type it in, get your answer, and carry on right where you were.
- Q: Where do the exchange rates come from?
  A: From the European Central Bank, refreshed once a day. The line under the amounts shows the rate and its date, and Settings updates the rates on demand. Your own currency, USD and EUR are free; Pro adds every pair among 30+ currencies. The daily cache keeps it working offline.
- Q: What is free, and what does Pro add?
  A: The floating calculator, length units, currency conversion between your own currency, USD and EUR, your last 5 calculations, 3 opacity steps and the default theme are free, with ads. Pro removes the ads and adds every unit category and currency pair, up to 100 history entries, 7 more themes and fine control of opacity, size and width — monthly, yearly or as a one-time lifetime purchase.

Page: https://codedac.com/apps/floatcalc.html
Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.floatcalc

## FloatCrypto+ (Android)

Keep Bitcoin, Ethereum and your altcoins on screen — above whatever app you are using.

FloatCrypto+ floats a live crypto ticker on top of every app, so you can check the market while you watch YouTube, read the news or reply to messages — no switching, no reloading. Drag it anywhere, resize it and dial the opacity down so it never gets in the way. Set an upper or lower target and it notifies you the moment the market crosses it, keep a watchlist of the coins you actually follow, and open 1-day, 7-day and 30-day charts with period high, low, open and change. Prices come from Binance with an automatic fallback, so the ticker keeps working when one source is unreachable. Market data is delayed by up to 30 seconds — 10 seconds on Pro — and is for reference only, not investment advice.

Features:
- Floating price ticker on top of every app — drag it anywhere, resize it, dial the opacity down
- Price alerts on an upper or lower target, added straight from the coin card with the coin filled in
- Watchlist of the coins you care about, with live price, 24-hour change and drag-to-reorder
- 1-day / 7-day / 30-day charts with period high, low, open and change
- Eastern and Western color modes — green-up/red-down, or red-up/blue-down as read in Korea, Japan and China
- Binance prices with an automatic fallback source, delayed by up to 30 seconds (10 on Pro)

FAQ:
- Q: Can I see prices while using other apps?
  A: Yes. The ticker floats on top of every app, so you can watch the market while you are on YouTube, in a game or in a chat — no switching, no reloading. Drag it anywhere, resize it, and lower the opacity so it never covers what you are reading.
- Q: How do price alerts work?
  A: Set an upper or lower target and FloatCrypto+ notifies you the moment the market crosses it. You can add an alert straight from a coin card — tap ⋮ and the coin is already filled in — and a bell badge marks every coin you are watching for.
- Q: What do I get for free?
  A: Free follows 2 coins with 1 price alert and the 1-day chart, with ads. Pro gives up to 10 coins, unlimited alerts, 7-day and 30-day charts, a 10-second refresh instead of 30 seconds and no ads — monthly, yearly or as a one-time lifetime purchase.

Page: https://codedac.com/apps/floatcrypto.html
Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.floatcrypto

## FloatTimer+ (Android)

A countdown timer, tally counter, and stopwatch that floats on top of every app.

FloatTimer+ is a floating overlay app that keeps a countdown timer, tally counter, and stopwatch on top of any app you use. Your timer stays visible while you do something else — drag it anywhere on screen, set size, opacity, and background color per item, or collapse it into a bubble marked with the app icon that reopens wherever you tap it. Shrink that bubble to the icon alone, or push it to the screen edge and it tucks half out of view until you want it back. Play, pause, and reset right on the floating timer, with a bar showing the time left, and drag it onto the X at the bottom of the screen to close it; everything keeps running in the background even when you switch apps or lock the screen. A home screen widget floats and starts any timer with one tap. Set it once and keep cooking, exercising, studying, or gaming without ever losing sight of the time.

Features:
- Floating overlay — timers, counters, and stopwatches float on any app; drag them anywhere and set size, opacity, and background color per item
- Multi-timer — any hours/minutes/seconds countdown, with 1, 5, 10, 25, 30 and 60-minute quick presets and as many timers running at once as you like; a home screen widget floats and starts any timer in one tap
- Overlay controls — play, pause, and reset right on the floating timer, with a bar for the time left; drag it onto the X to close it, or collapse it to a bubble marked with the app icon and tap anywhere on it to open it again
- Tally counter — tap to count up or down right on the overlay, with a step of 1, 2, 5, or 10 and as many counters as you need
- Stopwatch — several stopwatches, each timed separately; start, pause, and reset without leaving your current app
- Alerts and backup — sound, vibration, or a full-screen alert when time is up, plus file export and restore that merges or replaces

FAQ:
- Q: Does the timer stay visible while I use other apps?
  A: Yes. The timer, counter, and stopwatch float on top of any app and run in the background, so they keep going even when you switch apps or lock the screen.
- Q: Can I use it as a Pomodoro or workout timer?
  A: Yes. Quick presets include 25 minutes, you can set any duration you like, and you can run several timers at once for work and rest rounds. Pro repeats a timer 2, 3, or 5 times, or endlessly.
- Q: What does the free version include?
  A: Unlimited timers, counters and stopwatches with sound and vibration alerts, plus the home screen widget. The free version shows two floating timers at a time; Pro adds a full-screen alert even with the screen off, your own alarm sound and vibration, auto-repeat, as many floating timers at once as you like, and no ads.
- Q: Can I use FloatTimer+ on an Android car head unit?
  A: Yes, if your head unit has Google Play and runs Android 8.0 or later. The floating timer stays on top of navigation or music. The setup screens are laid out for wide, short landscape displays. The head unit must allow “Display over other apps”.

Page: https://codedac.com/apps/floattimer.html
Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.floattimer

## VolumeBooster+ (Android)

Louder in one tap — level buttons raise your device volume and boost most apps, up to 225%.

Is your phone too quiet? VolumeBooster+ raises the system output rather than one app, so quiet speakers, low earphones, hard-to-hear videos, music and games come through clearly. Tap a level — 100%, 125%, 150% or Max — and it turns up your device volume first, then adds the boost on top, up to 225% (+15 dB). The main screen shows your device volume next to the boost, and the volume buttons keep controlling your phone. Safe, Caution and Danger colors based on WHO hearing guidance show how far you have pushed it. Free reaches 183% (+10 dB); Pro opens 225%. A Loudness Maximizer, a 5-band equalizer whose nine presets are all free, a bass booster, a 3D virtualizer and AutoEQ correction built on 2,456 measured headphone profiles all live in the same app.

Features:
- One-tap levels 100%, 125%, 150% and Max: each raises your device volume, then boosts most apps up to 225% (+15 dB) — 183% free, 225% with Pro
- Device volume slider right on the main screen, and the volume buttons control your device volume — so a low phone volume never hides the boost
- Loudness Maximizer with multiband compression, makeup gain and an always-on peak limiter — louder, with no clipping
- Equalizer tab with a 5-band equalizer and 9 presets, all free, plus Bass Booster, 3D Virtualizer and AutoEQ — 2,456 measured headphone profiles, mainstream brands (Apple, Samsung, Sony, Bose, JBL, Beats) free
- Floating panel over any app with the same levels in its menu, hearing protection stats (Pro), a sleep timer with fade-out, L/R balance, a Quick Settings tile, a home-screen widget and notification controls
- Safe, Caution and Danger colors based on WHO hearing guidance show how far you have pushed the volume

FAQ:
- Q: Does it really make my phone louder?
  A: Yes. A level button first raises your device volume — to the maximum on the speaker, to 60% with headphones — and then adds the boost on top, through a Loudness Maximizer with multiband compression and makeup gain. It raises the whole system output, so music, videos, YouTube and games get louder together. If it still sounds quiet, check the device volume on the main screen; the built-in help can also switch to compatibility mode.
- Q: Is it actually free, or do I need a subscription?
  A: Free gives you up to 183% (+10 dB), all 9 presets, the 5-band equalizer, the floating panel and AutoEQ for mainstream brands like Apple, Samsung, Sony, Bose, JBL and Beats, with ads. Pro unlocks 225% (+15 dB), every AutoEQ profile and the hearing protection dashboard, and removes the ads — monthly, yearly or as a one-time lifetime purchase.
- Q: What do 150% and 225% mean?
  A: They name the boost levels: 100% is your normal sound, 125% adds 3 dB, 150% adds 6 dB, and 225% is the full +15 dB. The exact dB is shown under the big number. It is an estimate based on your system volume and the applied gain; real loudness varies by device, headphones and content. The app is not a medical device, so if you notice ear pain or ringing, lower the volume and consult a professional.
- Q: Can I use VolumeBooster+ on an Android car head unit?
  A: Yes, if your head unit has Google Play and runs Android 7.0 or later. The setup screens are laid out for wide, short landscape displays. How much louder it gets depends on the head unit's own amplifier and speakers.

Page: https://codedac.com/apps/volumebooster.html
Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.volumebooster

## PhotoCleaner+ (Android)

Hide personal info in photos and PDFs with a solid mask, entirely on your device.

PhotoCleaner+ hides personal information in photos and PDFs entirely on your device. It covers sensitive areas with a solid, opaque mask (not a blur or mosaic, so covered areas can't be recovered) and exports a clean copy. A built-in detector suggests likely sensitive text such as ID numbers, cards, phone numbers and emails — free and unlimited — but you draw and adjust the masks by hand and decide exactly what gets hidden. Photos, ID cards and multi-page PDFs are all handled, every saved or shared copy is re-encoded with no EXIF, and no gallery or storage permission is ever requested. Detection, editing and masking stay unlimited on the free version and no export ever carries a watermark; free exports 3 times a day, while Pro lifts that limit and adds PDF export, printing and any mask color. Turn on “Choose where to save” and you pick the folder and file name yourself.

Features:
- Solid opaque mask that can't be recovered (not a blur or mosaic)
- Draw masks by hand, then move, resize or delete them, with zoom for precision
- Built-in detection suggests likely sensitive text (ID numbers, cards, phones, emails) — free and unlimited, as a starting point you review
- Mask photos, ID cards and multi-page PDF documents
- Zero permissions, an EXIF & GPS notice, and every saved or shared copy re-encoded with no EXIF
- No watermark for anyone: 3 exports a day on free, unlimited with Pro along with PDF export and printing

FAQ:
- Q: Is the masking a blur or mosaic?
  A: No. Masking uses one style only, a solid opaque fill, and covered areas can't be recovered. With Pro you can pick any mask color.
- Q: Are my photos uploaded anywhere?
  A: No. Everything runs offline on your device and no photo is ever uploaded. The app also never requests gallery or storage permission.
- Q: Can I rely on auto-detection alone before exporting?
  A: Detection is only a starting point that suggests likely sensitive text. Always review the suggestions and add or remove masks yourself before exporting.
- Q: How many times can I export for free?
  A: Three times a day. What counts is the Export button, whatever you do with the result: save, share, PDF or print. Detection, editing and masking are never capped. Pro removes the daily limit.

Page: https://codedac.com/apps/photocleaner.html
Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.photocleaner

## ReadFocus+ (Android)

A dyslexia & ADHD reading aid: line highlight and reading mask keep your eyes on track and ease eye strain.

ReadFocus+ is a reading ruler, reading mask and reading aid for dyslexia and ADHD on Android. Grant the overlay permission once and a translucent focus strip floats on top of any app — ebook readers, browsers, PDF, news, comics — keeping your eyes on the line you're reading. It reduces skipping or re-reading the same row, easing eye strain and boosting reading concentration and efficiency.

Features:
- Line Highlight (Reading Ruler): illuminates your current line to keep eyes on track
- Reading Mask: dims everything except your reading zone for tunnel-vision focus
- Fully adjustable focus strip: height (50dp–300dp) and opacity (10%–100%)
- 10 color themes (3 free + 7 Pro)
- Works on top of any app — ebooks, PDF, webtoons, news, research papers
- Pro: no ads, 7 more color themes, and keep screen on while reading

FAQ:
- Q: How does ReadFocus+ work?
  A: Grant the overlay permission once and a semi-transparent focus strip floats on top of any app. Drag it to the line you're reading and your eyes stay on track instead of wandering or skipping rows.
- Q: Which apps does it work with?
  A: It works on top of any app on screen — ebook and PDF readers, research papers, web articles, blogs, news, study notes, textbooks, comics, webtoons, and long emails or chat history.
- Q: Is it free to use?
  A: Yes. The free version includes both focus modes, 3 color themes and strip height and opacity adjustment, with ads. Pro removes the ads and adds 7 more color themes and Keep Screen On — monthly, yearly or as a one-time lifetime purchase.

Page: https://codedac.com/apps/readfocus.html
Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.readfocus

## FloatNote+ (Android)

Sticky notes that float over any app! Jot down a thought and it stays on your screen, always one tap away.

FloatNote+ keeps sticky notes floating on top of any app. Grant the overlay permission once and every note lives as a small chip above your browser, chat, video or home screen; tap it and the chip expands into a full card you can read, edit and share on the spot. Colors, rich text and inline images keep each note distinct, while the main app works as a library for searching, pinning and reordering. Light and dark themes are both included. Pair it with FloatNote+ for Windows and notes written on your phone show up on your PC, and notes written on your PC show up on your phone. You just sign in to Google Drive with the same account in both apps, and your notes never pass through a CodeDAC server — they are stored only in your own Google Drive.

Features:
- Floating overlay notes: collapse a note to a chip, expand it to a full card over any app
- 7 sticky-note colors and rich text: bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, text color and size
- Inline images (Pro): attach photos right inside a note
- Note reminders — once, every day, weekdays or chosen days
- Library with instant search, pinning and drag-to-reorder — dragging a chip to the bottom zone stashes the note instead of deleting it
- Pro: unlimited floating notes, inline images, Google Drive sync, unlimited reminders, no ads

FAQ:
- Q: How do floating notes work?
  A: Grant the overlay permission once and your notes float above other apps as small chips. Tap a chip to expand it into a card and edit it right there; tap outside and it collapses back, saving automatically. Dragging a chip to the zone at the bottom of the screen only stashes the note — real deletion always asks for confirmation.
- Q: Where can I use it?
  A: Anywhere on screen — over a browser, a chat, a video, a document or the home screen. You can also create a note without opening the app: from the share sheet, from text you select in another app, or from the Quick Settings tile. The home screen widget shows your notes, and a tap floats one.
- Q: Does it sync with my Windows PC?
  A: Yes. Install FloatNote+ for Windows as well, then in the settings of both apps sign in to Google Drive with the same account and turn on automatic sync. Notes written on your phone then show up on your PC, and notes written on your PC show up on your phone. Your notes never pass through a CodeDAC server — they are stored only in your own Google Drive. Both the note text and the images attached to it travel between devices.
- Q: Is it free?
  A: Yes. Saving notes is unlimited and free, and the free version floats one note at a time and gives you all 7 colors, adjustable opacity, export and import and the home screen widget, with ads. Pro adds unlimited floating notes, inline images, Google Drive sync and unlimited reminders, and removes ads.
- Q: Can I use FloatNote+ on an Android car head unit?
  A: Yes, if your head unit has Google Play and runs Android 8.0 or later. Notes float on top of navigation or music. The setup screens are laid out for wide, short landscape displays. The head unit must allow “Display over other apps”.
- Q: Can a note pop up at a set time?
  A: Yes. Set a time and your note pops up on screen with a notification — once, every day, on weekdays, or only on the days you pick. (Free: 1 reminder · Pro: unlimited)

Page: https://codedac.com/apps/floatnote.html
Store: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.codedac.floatnote

## Clipboard+ for Windows (Windows)

A Windows tray clipboard manager that syncs with your Android phone through your own Google Drive.

Clipboard+ for Windows is a tray-resident clipboard manager that automatically saves the text and images you copy. Everything is recorded the moment you copy it, so even if you overwrite something by accident you can pull the earlier item back and paste it. A global hotkey opens a quick-pick popup right where your cursor is: pick a clip with Ctrl+1–9 and Enter pastes it into whatever you were typing in, without leaving the window. Pair it with the Android Clipboard+ app and what you copy on your phone pastes on your PC, and what you copy on your PC pastes on your phone. Your clips never pass through a CodeDAC server — they are stored only in your own Google Drive. Saved items can be organized into groups and snippets and searched.

Features:
- Sits in the tray and saves text and images the moment you copy them — it never has to keep checking in the background, so it stays light
- Bidirectional phone-to-PC sync through your own Google Drive
- Android-style UI with light/dark themes, group sidebar, snippets, and pin/copy/edit/search
- Multi-select bulk move, delete, and merge, newest/oldest sorting, and a full-size image viewer
- Quick-pick popup at the cursor on a global hotkey, plus hotkeys to open the window and capture text selected in other apps, and run-at-startup
- Export/import compatible with the Android Clipboard+ backup format, plus PDF export

FAQ:
- Q: Does it sync with the Android Clipboard+ app?
  A: Yes. Turn on sync with the same Google account on both devices, and what you copy on your phone pastes on your PC, and what you copy on your PC pastes on your phone. Your clips never pass through a CodeDAC server — they travel only through your own Google Drive.
- Q: Where is my clipboard data stored, and is it safe?
  A: Your clip history is kept on your PC by default (in the %APPDATA%\ClipboardPlus folder). If you turn on sync, it is also stored in a private app area of your own Google Drive — an area that stays hidden from your Drive view and cannot be opened by anything other than Clipboard+. The app uses only that private area, so it cannot reach any of your other photos or documents on Drive.
- Q: What is free, and what does Pro add?
  A: The clipboard history, snippets and groups, search, the quick-pick popup, and the light and dark themes are all free. Pro adds Google Drive sync, copying image clips back to the clipboard, PDF export, backup import, unlimited groups, and unlimited image storage — free image storage is capped at 50 MB.

Page: https://codedac.com/apps/clipboardwin.html
Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9N9SRKQV1R6D

## ReadFocus+ for Windows (Windows)

A tray-resident focus strip for Windows: Mask or Highlight keeps your eyes on the line, and every click passes straight through to the app underneath.

ReadFocus+ for Windows is the desktop version of the Android ReadFocus+ app. It lays a calm focus strip over whatever you are reading — a web page, a PDF, a document, code — so it is easier to stay on the line. Mask gently dims the top and bottom of the screen and leaves a clear band across the middle; Highlight marks the line you are on with a soft tinted strip. The Focus Strip is click-through, so you keep scrolling, selecting and clicking underneath exactly as before, and a small floating panel switches modes, moves or locks the band and hides it away without making you leave what you are reading.

Features:
- Two reading modes — Mask dims everything outside a clear band, Highlight marks the line you are on
- Click-through: keep scrolling, selecting and clicking the app underneath — nothing intercepts your mouse
- A floating panel to switch mode, move or lock the strip and hide it, collapsing to a single row when you do not need it
- Keyboard shortcuts for start and stop, mode, show and hide, lock, and nudging the strip up or down
- Multi-monitor: the reading band follows the panel to whichever screen you move it to, and waits in the system tray until you need it
- No ads. Pro is a one-time purchase: premium themes and Keep Screen On

FAQ:
- Q: Is this the same app as ReadFocus+ on Android?
  A: It is the same app built for Windows, with the same two reading modes. The two are bought separately on their own stores, and there is nothing to sync — ReadFocus+ never stores what you read.
- Q: Which apps does it work with?
  A: Any app on screen: browsers, PDF and ebook readers, documents, code editors, research papers, and long emails or chat logs. The Focus Strip is drawn on top of the screen, so the app underneath does not have to support anything.
- Q: Is it free to use?
  A: Yes. The free version includes both reading modes, Focus Strip height and opacity, and three of the ten themes. Pro is a one-time purchase — not a subscription — and adds premium themes and Keep Screen On. The Windows version has no ads.

Page: https://codedac.com/apps/readfocuswin.html
Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9NMSHKKX3R5C

## FloatNote+ for Windows (Windows)

Sticky notes that float on top of whatever you are working in: write without leaving the window you are in, and they never steal its focus.

FloatNote+ for Windows is the desktop version of the Android FloatNote+ app. Every note lives as a small chip above your browser, your editor or your spreadsheet; click it and it expands into a card right there, ready to read or edit, and the arrow at the top or Esc folds it back into a chip. A chip never takes focus from the app behind it, so whatever you were typing stays exactly as it was — and there is no save button, since every keystroke is committed for you. Seven pastel colors, rich text and inline images keep notes apart, a library window handles search, pinning and management, and optional sync moves your notes through an app-private folder in your own Google Drive, the same one the Android app uses.

Features:
- Sticky notes that float above every window: a chip expands into an editable card in place, and Esc folds it back
- Never steals focus — drag or click a chip and your cursor stays in the app you were typing in
- Note reminders — once, every day, weekdays or chosen days
- Rich text — bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, text color and size — with 7 pastel note colors and inline images
- Bidirectional phone-to-PC sync through your own Google Drive — the same app-private folder the Android app uses, and never a CodeDAC server
- Global hotkeys, system tray, light and dark themes, run at logon, 21 languages. No ads, and every feature is free

FAQ:
- Q: Is this the same app as FloatNote+ on Android?
  A: It is the same app built for Windows, with the same chips and cards. Once you sign in to Google Drive with the same account in both apps and turn on automatic sync, notes written on the PC show up on the phone and notes written on the phone show up on the PC. Your notes never pass through a CodeDAC server — they are stored only in your own Google Drive. Both the note text and the images attached to it travel between devices.
- Q: Does it get in the way of the app underneath?
  A: No. A chip is a floating window that never takes focus, so clicking or dragging one leaves your cursor exactly where you were typing. Click a chip to expand the card, click the arrow at the top, press Esc or click elsewhere and it folds back, already saved.
- Q: Is it free to use?
  A: Yes. Every feature of the Windows version is free — as many floating notes as you like, inline images, note transparency, Google Drive sync, and export and import. No in-app purchases, no ads, no account. (On the phone side, sync is a Pro feature of the Android app.)
- Q: Can a note pop up at a set time?
  A: Yes. Pick a time and the note comes up on screen with a notification: once, every day, on weekdays, or only on the days you choose.

## FloatTimer+ for Windows (Windows)

Timers, counters and stopwatches that float on top of whatever you are working in: small pastel cards you drag where you want them, and they never steal focus from the app underneath.

FloatTimer+ for Windows is the desktop version of the Android FloatTimer+ app. Instead of a window you have to switch to, each timer becomes a small pastel card floating above your work — your editor, your browser, your video call — counting down in plain sight. Click a card to start or pause it, drag it wherever it belongs, or collapse it into a bubble barely bigger than a button and marked with the app icon — click anywhere on it to open the card again, shrink it to the icon alone, or push it against the screen edge where it tucks half out of view. The card never takes focus from the app behind it, so your cursor stays exactly where you left it while you type. Counters add and subtract with a click on either half, stopwatches count up, and nine pastel colors keep them apart. It lives in the system tray, needs no account and never touches the network — your timers stay in a file on your own PC.

Features:
- Timers, counters and stopwatches float above every window as small pastel cards — drag one anywhere, resize it, or collapse it to a bubble marked with the app icon
- Never steals focus — click or drag a card and your cursor stays in the document you were typing in
- Start, pause and restart with the ▶/⏸/↻ button on the card itself without opening the app, and timers show a bar of the time left; counters add and subtract with a click on either half
- Nine pastel colors, adjustable card size and opacity, and app windows that follow your light or dark theme
- The backup file is the same format as the Android app, so you can export on one and restore on the other
- Global hotkeys, system tray, run at logon, 21 languages. No account, no network, no ads — and Pro is a one-time purchase

- Q: Does it get in the way of the app underneath?
  A: No. A card is a floating window that never takes focus, so clicking or dragging it leaves your cursor exactly where you were typing. When you want the screen back, collapse a card into a bubble barely bigger than a button, push it against the screen edge to tuck it half out of view, or hide every card at once with a hotkey.
- Q: Is it free to use?
  A: Yes. You can make as many timers, counters and stopwatches as you like — the list is never limited — and the Windows version has no ads. The free version floats two cards on screen at a time. Pro is a one-time purchase — not a subscription — and adds full-screen alerts and your own alert sound, repeating timers, unlimited floating cards and any color you like.

## PhotoCleaner+ for Windows (Windows)

Find personal info in photos, screenshots and PDFs, check every box, and export a solidly masked copy with no metadata — all on your PC.

PhotoCleaner+ for Windows is the desktop version of the Android PhotoCleaner+ app. Open a photo, a screenshot or a PDF — or paste one with Ctrl+V, drag it onto the window, or right-click it in File Explorer and choose "Clean with PhotoCleaner+" — and detection starts on its own. It boxes likely personal info such as phone numbers, emails, card numbers, IBAN, passport numbers and the MRZ, Korean IDs, names, addresses and license plates, faces (frontal faces work best) and QR codes, plus any words you set to always hide. Detection is a starting point, not a guarantee: click a box to turn it on or off, drag to move or resize it, and draw your own over anything that was missed. Text is read by the recognition languages installed in Windows, so Korean documents need the Korean language installed. Export covers every box with a solid, opaque mask — not a blur — and the result screen lets you Save as JPEG or PNG, Copy, Share, Save PDF or Print. Saved copies are encoded fresh from the pixels, so no EXIF, GPS location or capture time comes along; your original is never modified, and there is no watermark. Everything runs on your PC with no account and no upload, and the app keeps no list of recent files.

Features:
- Finds phone numbers, emails, card numbers, IBAN, passport numbers and MRZ, Korean IDs, names, addresses, license plates, faces and QR codes
- Review every box before export: click to toggle, drag to move, drag an edge to resize, draw your own, Undo any step
- Open photos, screenshots and PDFs by drag and drop, Ctrl+V, or right-click "Clean with PhotoCleaner+" in File Explorer
- Solid, opaque masks — not a blur — and no watermark; Save as JPEG or PNG, Copy, Share, Save PDF and Print
- Saved copies carry no EXIF, GPS location or other metadata, and your original is never overwritten
- Fully on your PC: no account, no upload, no recent-files list. Light and dark theme, 21 languages

FAQ:

  A: It is the same idea built for Windows: find personal info, check the boxes, export a solidly masked copy. Detection uses the text and face recognition built into Windows instead of the phone's, so results are similar but not identical. Each version is installed from its own store.
- Q: Will it find every piece of personal info?
  A: No tool can promise that. Detection is a starting point: always check the masking before you export and draw a box over anything that was missed. Text is read with the recognition languages installed in Windows — Korean IDs, names and addresses need the Korean language installed, and the Settings screen shows which languages you have.
- Q: Are my files uploaded, or is the original changed?
  A: Neither. Detection, masking and export all run on your PC with no account and nothing uploaded. Masking works on a copy, the app refuses to save over the original, and saved copies are encoded fresh so they carry none of the original's metadata.
- Q: What is free, and what does Pro add?
  A: Finding personal info is free and unlimited, and you can save, copy or share the masked copy of 3 documents a day for free. Pro is a one-time purchase that removes the daily limit and adds PDF export, printing, the always-hide list and your choice of mask color. There are no ads and no watermark, on either version.

## FloatCrypto+ for Windows (Windows)

Bitcoin, Ethereum and your altcoins in a slim strip on top of every window — the market in the corner of your eye while you work, without ever stealing focus.

FloatCrypto+ for Windows is the desktop version of the Android FloatCrypto+ app. It keeps a slim price ticker on top of every window — your browser, your documents, your video call — showing each coin's symbol and 24-hour change, colored by direction. No tab to switch to, no page to reload. Drag the ticker anywhere, adjust its opacity and text size, or collapse it into a small bubble that tucks against the edge of the screen; it never takes focus from the app you are typing in. Hover the tray icon for a full table of prices, even with the ticker turned off. Set a target above or below the current price and get a desktop notification the moment the market crosses it, one-time or repeating. Pick coins from the hundreds of pairs traded on Binance, drag them into your own order, and double-click any coin for a chart with the period high, low, open and change. Prices come from Binance's public market data with automatic fallback to alternate servers and CoinGecko, may be delayed by up to 30 seconds, and are for information only — FloatCrypto+ is not a trading app and nothing in it is investment advice.

Features:

- Watchlist from the hundreds of Binance pairs, drag-to-reorder, and 1-day, 7-day and 30-day charts with period high, low, open and change
- Western (green up, red down) or Eastern (red up, blue down) colors, and a full price table on the tray icon
- Global hotkeys, system tray, start with Windows, light and dark themes, 21 languages. No ads, no account

FAQ:
- Q: Is this the same app as FloatCrypto+ on Android?

- Q: Does the ticker get in the way of what I am doing?
  A: No. The ticker is a floating strip that never takes focus, so clicking or dragging it leaves your cursor exactly where you were typing. Lower its opacity, shrink the text, collapse it into a bubble that tucks against the screen edge, or hide it with Ctrl+Alt+T — and the tray icon still shows every price when you hover over it.

# Guides

## How to see your clipboard history on Android

Android itself remembers only the last thing you copied — copy something new and the previous text is gone. If you want to get back an address, a code or a sentence you copied earlier, you need a place that keeps a history. There are two: your keyboard, and a clipboard manager app.

### Option 1: the clipboard in your keyboard

Many keyboards have their own clipboard. In Gboard, tap the clipboard icon in the toolbar above the keys (turn it on the first time). Samsung Keyboard has a clipboard button in its toolbar too.

This is the quickest way to grab something you copied a few minutes ago. The catch is that keyboard clipboards are short-term: Gboard, for example, removes unpinned items after about an hour, and you only see the list while you are typing.

### Option 2: a clipboard manager that keeps a real history

If you copy the same things again and again — addresses, account numbers, canned replies — a clipboard manager keeps them until you delete them, lets you search them, and can show them over any app.

Clipboard+ (our app) keeps the text and images you copy in a history, newest first, with search and a floating panel you can open over the app you are using.

One catch: since Android 10, only the app on screen (and the keyboard you're typing with) can read the clipboard. Clipboard+ gets around waiting for you with an optional Auto-save: turn it on in Settings and, with a one-time Accessibility permission, everything you copy is saved the moment you copy it. Without Auto-save, bring the app to the front right after you copy.

1. Install Clipboard+ from Google Play and open it once.
2. Turn on Auto-save in Settings (optional) and copies are saved automatically. Otherwise, save right after you copy: tap the floating bubble at the edge of the screen, tap the save button on the home-screen widget, or open the app. For text, selecting it in another app and choosing Clipboard+ from the selection menu always works, because it skips the clipboard entirely.
3. Open the floating panel (or the app) to see your history, tap a clip to copy it again, and paste it where you are.
4. Keep things you reuse as snippets in groups, so they are always one tap away.

### Which one should you use?

For a one-off — pasting something you copied a minute ago — the keyboard clipboard is enough. If you lose clips you wanted, or you keep retyping the same text, a clipboard manager saves that time. Clipboard+ is free to start; Pro adds sync with the Windows app through your own Google Drive, unlimited image clips and PDF export.

- Q: Does Android have a built-in clipboard history?
  A: Not in the system itself — Android keeps only the latest clip. Keyboards such as Gboard and Samsung Keyboard add a short-term clipboard list.
- Q: Can I see clipboard history from my phone on my PC?
  A: Yes, with Clipboard+ on both: the Android app and Clipboard+ for Windows sync through your own Google Drive (a Pro feature on Android).
- Q: I granted every permission, but not everything I copy gets saved.
  A: That's the privacy rule Android introduced in version 10: an app that isn't on screen can't read the clipboard, and ordinary permissions don't change that. Turn on Auto-save in Clipboard+ Settings — it uses the Accessibility service to save each copy as you make it. Otherwise save right after copying with the bubble, the widget or by opening the app, or use Clipboard+ in the text selection menu. The system clipboard only holds the last item, so without Auto-save, copying something else first means the earlier item is gone.

Page: https://codedac.com/guides/android-clipboard-history.html

## How to open an app automatically after a reboot on Android (no root)

Android does not have a setting that opens an app when the phone starts. If you open the same apps after every restart — a navigation app in the car, a launcher on a kiosk tablet, a music app on a head unit — an auto-start app can do it for you.

### Why it doesn't happen on its own

Since Android 10, apps are not allowed to open screens from the background on their own. An app that should open others after a reboot therefore needs the "Display over other apps" permission, and it can only start them once the phone has been unlocked for the first time.

### Set it up with AutoStart+

AutoStart+ (our app) opens the apps you pick after every restart, as soon as you unlock the phone. It needs no root.

1. Install AutoStart+ from Google Play and open it.
2. Tap Add apps and choose the apps you want to open after a reboot. Drag the rows to set which one opens first.
3. Allow "Display over other apps" when asked — without it Android blocks the launch.
4. Tap Test it now to see what will happen, without restarting the phone.
5. Restart the phone and unlock it: your apps open in the order you set.

### Car head units and devices that sleep

Many Android head units don't really reboot — they go to sleep when the car is off. AutoStart+ has a Car Mode that opens your apps again every time the screen wakes up.

- Q: Do I need root to auto start apps on Android?
  A: No. AutoStart+ works without root; it only needs the "Display over other apps" permission.
- Q: Why don't my apps open before I unlock the phone?
  A: Android does not let apps open others until the phone has been unlocked once after a reboot. Your apps open right after you unlock.
- Q: How many apps can I auto start for free?
  A: The free version starts 1 app per boot. Pro starts your whole list in order.

Page: https://codedac.com/guides/open-app-automatically-after-reboot-android.html

## How to keep a note on top of other apps on Android

Copying a list into a form, checking a recipe while a video plays, keeping an order number in view in a chat — switching back and forth to your notes app breaks the flow. A floating note stays on screen over whatever app you are using.

### How floating notes work

A floating note is a small window drawn over other apps. Android allows this through the "Display over other apps" permission, which you grant once. The note stays on top while you keep using the app underneath.

### Set it up with FloatNote+

FloatNote+ (our app) floats each note as a small chip over any app. Tap the chip and it opens as a card right there; tap its title bar to fold it back.

1. Install FloatNote+ from Google Play and allow "Display over other apps".
2. Tap + to write a note — it appears over your screen as a card.
3. Open the app you need. The note stays on top; fold it into a chip when you want the screen back.
4. Use colors, bold, text size and pictures to make notes easy to tell apart.
5. To bring a note up at a set time, open its ⋮ menu and choose Remind me — once, every day, weekdays or the days you pick.

### Also on your PC

FloatNote+ for Windows floats the same kind of notes over any window, and the two apps sync through your own Google Drive (a Pro feature on Android).

- Q: Does Android have floating notes built in?
  A: Android has no general floating-note feature. Apps like FloatNote+ add it using the "Display over other apps" permission.
- Q: Can a note pop up at a set time?
  A: Yes. In FloatNote+, set a reminder from the note's ⋮ menu and the note comes up on screen with a notification. The free version keeps one reminder; Pro has no limit.
- Q: Is FloatNote+ free?
  A: Saving notes is free and unlimited, and the free version floats one note at a time. Pro adds unlimited floating notes, inline images, Google Drive sync and no ads.

Page: https://codedac.com/guides/floating-notes-over-other-apps-android.html

## How to keep a timer on screen while using other apps on Android

The timer in the Clock app runs in the background, but you can't see it while you are in another app — you have to pull down notifications or switch back. For studying with a lecture, timing a presentation, or a game, it helps to have the time on screen the whole time.

FloatTimer+ (our app) floats timers, stopwatches and tally counters over any app as small cards you can drag anywhere.

4. Fold it into a bubble when you need the space; the time keeps running.

### More than one at a time

You can make as many timers, counters and stopwatches as you like for free, and they keep running. The free version shows two on screen at a time; Pro floats as many as you want at once.

  A: Yes. A floating timer stays on top of any app, including videos and games, once you allow "Display over other apps".

## How to hide personal info in a screenshot before you share it

Screenshots and photos of documents often carry more than you meant to share: a phone number, an ID or card number, an address, a face, a QR code. Before posting or sending them, cover that information properly.

### What to avoid

A semi-transparent highlighter or thin pen strokes can leave text readable once someone raises the contrast, and blur or mosaic on small text can sometimes be guessed. Use a solid, opaque box over anything private, and share a copy rather than the original.

### Option 1: your phone's photo editor

Most gallery apps have a markup or drawing tool. If you use it, pick a solid shape or a fully opaque pen, cover each item completely, and zoom in to check the edges before you save.

### Option 2: PhotoCleaner+

PhotoCleaner+ (our app) is made for this job. It suggests likely personal information, you review each box, and it exports a copy with solid masks — everything runs on your phone, nothing is uploaded.

1. Open a photo, screenshot or PDF in PhotoCleaner+.
2. Check the suggested boxes — phone numbers, emails, card numbers and similar text — and add your own by drawing.
3. Move, resize or delete boxes until everything private is covered.
4. Export the masked copy and share that. Your original is not changed, and saved copies carry no EXIF or GPS data.

- Q: Is blurring enough to hide a phone number?
  A: Not always. Light blur on small text can sometimes be read or guessed. A solid, opaque mask is the safe choice.
- Q: Does PhotoCleaner+ upload my photos?
  A: No. Detection and masking run on your phone, and your photos and documents are never uploaded.
- Q: Is it free?
  A: Detection, editing and masking are free; you can export 3 times a day. Pro removes the daily limit and adds PDF export and printing.

Page: https://codedac.com/guides/hide-personal-info-in-screenshots.html

## How to keep a sticky note always on top on Windows

A sticky note is only useful if you can see it. On Windows, notes on the desktop usually end up behind the browser, document or spreadsheet you are working in, so you have to dig for them. There are two ways to keep a note on top.

### Option 1: pin a window with PowerToys

Microsoft PowerToys, a free set of utilities from Microsoft, includes Always On Top. Install PowerToys, turn on Always On Top, click the window you want to keep in front — for example a notes window — and press Win+Ctrl+T. Press it again to unpin.

This works for almost any window. The catch is that a pinned window is a full window: it takes focus when you click it, and it covers the same space whether you are reading the note or not.

### Option 2: notes that float by design

FloatNote+ for Windows (our app) keeps each note as a small chip above every window. Click the chip and it opens as a card right there; press Esc and it folds back. Chips never take focus from the app behind them, so your cursor stays where you were typing.

1. Install FloatNote+ from the Microsoft Store.
2. Create a note from the tray icon or with a global hotkey — it appears as a card over your screen.
3. Keep working: the note stays above every window. Click the arrow at the top or press Esc to fold it into a chip.
4. Drag chips anywhere, use colors and rich text to tell them apart, and set a reminder to bring a note up at a set time.

### Your notes on your phone too

FloatNote+ for Windows syncs with the FloatNote+ Android app through your own Google Drive, so a note you write on your PC is on your phone. Every feature of the Windows version is free.

- Q: Can Windows Sticky Notes stay on top of other windows?
  A: Not by themselves in most setups. You can pin any window, including a notes window, with PowerToys Always On Top (Win+Ctrl+T), or use an app whose notes float above other windows by design.
- Q: Does a floating note steal focus from what I'm typing?
  A: FloatNote+ chips don't. Clicking or dragging a chip leaves your cursor in the app you were using; only an opened card takes focus, because you type into it.

Page: https://codedac.com/guides/sticky-notes-always-on-top-windows.html

## How to see your clipboard history on Windows

Copy something new and the previous clip is gone — unless you keep a history. Windows 10 and 11 have one built in, and a clipboard manager can keep a longer one.

### Option 1: the built-in clipboard history (Win+V)

Press Win+V. The first time, Windows asks you to turn clipboard history on (you can also do it in Settings > System > Clipboard). After that, Win+V shows your recent clips, and clicking one pastes it.

It is quick, but limited: it keeps up to 25 items, and everything except pinned items is cleared when you restart the PC. There is no search, and it does not reach your phone.

### Option 2: a clipboard manager that keeps everything

Clipboard+ for Windows (our app) sits in the tray and saves the text and images you copy the moment you copy them. Your history stays until you delete it, and you can search it, organize it into groups and snippets, and pull it up with a hotkey.

1. Install Clipboard+ from the Microsoft Store; it starts in the system tray.
2. Copy as usual — every text and image clip is saved automatically.
3. Press the global hotkey to open the quick-pick popup at your cursor, pick a clip with Ctrl+1–9 and press Enter to paste it.
4. Open the window to search, pin, edit, or keep frequently used text as snippets.

### Between your phone and PC

Paired with the Clipboard+ Android app, what you copy on your phone pastes on your PC and the other way around, through your own Google Drive. Clipboard history, snippets, groups, search and the quick-pick popup are free; Pro adds sync, unlimited image storage and PDF export.

- Q: Why is my Win+V clipboard history empty after a restart?
  A: Windows clears clipboard history when the PC restarts, except for pinned items. A clipboard manager such as Clipboard+ keeps your history across restarts.
- Q: How many items does Windows clipboard history keep?
  A: Up to 25. Older items drop off as you copy new ones.

Page: https://codedac.com/guides/clipboard-history-windows.html

Timing a presentation, a focus session or a call is easier when the time stays in view. Windows offers one built-in way, and a floating-timer app adds more.

2. Create a timer, counter or stopwatch and float it.
3. Start, pause and reset from the card itself; drag it anywhere or resize it.

- Q: Does Windows have an always-on-top timer?
  A: The Clock app's Keep on top shows one timer in a small window above others. For several timers, counters or stopwatches at once, use a floating-timer app.

## Reading ruler for dyslexia and ADHD on Android: keep your place while reading

Long text on a phone screen is easy to get lost in: your eyes slip to the next line, skip a row, or come back to a sentence you already read. Many people with dyslexia or ADHD use a ruler or a card under the line when reading on paper. On a phone, a reading ruler does the same job on screen.

### Start with your display settings

Android's accessibility and display settings — larger font size, bold text, dark theme — can make text easier to read. They don't, however, mark the line you are on, which is what helps when your eyes keep wandering.

### Add a reading ruler with ReadFocus+

ReadFocus+ (our app) floats a focus strip on top of any app — ebooks, PDFs, browsers, news, webtoons. Choose Line Highlight to light up the line you are reading, or Reading Mask to dim everything except your reading zone.

1. Install ReadFocus+ from Google Play and allow "Display over other apps".
2. Pick a mode: Line Highlight (a reading ruler) or Reading Mask.
3. Open the app you're reading in and drag the strip to your line.
4. Adjust its height (50–300 dp), opacity and color theme until it feels comfortable.

### Free and Pro

The free version includes both focus modes, 3 color themes, and strip height and opacity adjustment. Pro removes the ads and adds all 10 themes and keep-screen-on.

- Q: Does a reading ruler help with dyslexia?
  A: Many readers with dyslexia or ADHD find that marking the current line makes it easier to keep their place. It is a reading aid, not a treatment — try it and keep the settings that feel comfortable.
- Q: Which apps does ReadFocus+ work with?
  A: Any app on screen: ebook and PDF readers, browsers, news, study notes, comics and webtoons.

Page: https://codedac.com/guides/reading-ruler-dyslexia-adhd-android.html

## How to use a reading ruler on Windows (for dyslexia and ADHD)

Reading long pages on a monitor makes it easy to lose the line. A reading ruler highlights the line you are on, or dims the rest of the screen, so your eyes stay on track.

### Option 1: Line focus in Microsoft Edge

Microsoft Edge has Immersive Reader, a clean reading view for web pages. In its reading preferences, Line focus highlights one, three or five lines at a time. It only works on pages that open in Immersive Reader, not in PDFs, documents or other apps.

### Option 2: a focus strip over any app

ReadFocus+ for Windows (our app) lays a focus strip over whatever you are reading — a web page, a PDF, a document, code. Mask dims the top and bottom of the screen and leaves a clear band; Highlight marks the line you are on. The strip is click-through, so you keep scrolling and clicking underneath as before.

1. Install ReadFocus+ from the Microsoft Store.
2. Start it from the floating panel or with a keyboard shortcut, and choose Mask or Highlight.
3. Move the strip to your line, or nudge it up and down with shortcuts as you read.
4. Lock it, hide it, or move it to another monitor from the panel.

### Free and Pro

The free version includes both modes, strip height and opacity settings, and three themes. Pro is a one-time purchase that adds premium themes and keep-screen-on. There are no ads.

- Q: Does Windows have a reading ruler?
  A: Edge's Immersive Reader has Line focus for web pages. For other apps — PDFs, Word, code editors — you need a screen overlay such as ReadFocus+ for Windows.
- Q: Will the strip block my clicks?
  A: No. ReadFocus+ for Windows is click-through: scrolling, selecting and clicking go to the app underneath.

Page: https://codedac.com/guides/reading-ruler-windows.html

## How to use a calculator on top of other apps on Android

Checking a price in a shopping app, splitting a bill in a chat, converting a currency while booking — switching to the Calculator app and back means losing your place and remembering numbers in your head. A floating calculator stays on screen over the app you are using.

### Option 1: split screen

Android can show two apps at once in split screen. Open the recent apps screen, choose split screen for one app and pick the Calculator for the other half. It works, but each app gets only half of the screen.

### Option 2: a floating calculator

FloatCalc+ (our app) is a calculator window that floats over any app. The calculator, unit converter and currency converter share one window and one keypad; drag it anywhere, and shrink it to an icon at the screen edge when you need the space.

1. Install FloatCalc+ from Google Play and allow "Display over other apps".
2. Open the floating calculator from the app, the Quick Settings tile or the home screen widget, and drag it where it doesn't cover what you need.
3. Type the expression on the keypad — the result appears as you type. To use a number from another app, select it and tap “Calculate with FloatCalc+”; copy the answer from the ⋮ menu.
4. Switch to the unit or currency converter in the same window. Exchange rates come from the European Central Bank, refresh daily and keep working offline.

### Free and Pro

The floating calculator, length units and currency conversion between your own currency, USD and EUR are free, with ads. Pro removes the ads and adds all unit categories, every currency pair and more themes.

- Q: Can I use a calculator without leaving my app?
  A: Yes. A floating calculator such as FloatCalc+ stays on top of other apps once you allow "Display over other apps".
- Q: Where do the exchange rates come from?
  A: From the European Central Bank, refreshed once a day and cached for offline use.

Page: https://codedac.com/guides/floating-calculator-over-other-apps-android.html

## How to see crypto prices while using other apps on Android

Exchange apps show prices inside the app or in a home-screen widget, so checking the market means leaving whatever you are doing. A floating ticker keeps the prices you follow on screen over any app.

### Set up a floating ticker with FloatCrypto+

FloatCrypto+ (our app) floats a price ticker over every app — YouTube, news, a game, a chat. Drag it anywhere, resize it and lower its opacity so it doesn't cover what you are reading.

1. Install FloatCrypto+ from Google Play and allow "Display over other apps".
2. Add the coins you follow to your watchlist and drag them into your order.
3. Turn on the floating ticker and place it where you like.
4. Set an upper or lower price alert from a coin's ⋮ menu to be notified when the market crosses it.

### Good to know

Prices come from Binance with an automatic fallback source and may be delayed by up to 30 seconds (10 seconds on Pro). They are for reference only, and the app does not trade or connect to an exchange account. Nothing here is investment advice.

Free follows 2 coins with 1 alert. Pro gives 10 coins, unlimited alerts, longer charts, a 10-second refresh and no ads.

- Q: Can I see crypto prices over YouTube or a game?
  A: Yes. The ticker floats on top of every app once you allow "Display over other apps".
- Q: Are the prices real-time?
  A: They may be delayed by up to 30 seconds (10 seconds on Pro) and are for reference only.

## How to make your Android phone louder

If videos, calls on speaker or music are too quiet, start with a few settings — sometimes the phone is simply limiting itself. If that isn't enough, a volume booster can raise the output further.

### Check these first

Make sure you are turning up the media volume, not the ringtone: press a volume button while a video is playing, or open the volume panel and raise the media slider.

Some phones have a media volume limit. On Samsung phones, look for Media volume limiter in the volume settings. Also try the phone's own sound effects or equalizer if it has one, and check whether a case is covering the speaker.

### Raise the output with VolumeBooster+

VolumeBooster+ (our app) raises the system output rather than one app's volume, so videos, music and games get louder. A boost only adds on top of your device volume, so its level buttons turn the device volume up first and then add the boost — and the main screen shows both.

1. Install VolumeBooster+ from Google Play and tap Start: your device volume goes up and the boost turns on at 150%.
2. Play something and pick another level if you need it — 100%, 125%, 150% or Max — or fine-tune with the slider, watching the Safe, Caution and Danger colors.
3. Use the equalizer presets, bass booster or AutoEQ for your headphones to make it clearer, not just louder.
4. Turn the boost down when you don't need it — your ears and speaker will thank you.

### Free and Pro, and your hearing

Free boosts up to 183% (+10 dB); Pro opens 225% (+15 dB). The dB value is an estimate, and the app is not a medical device — if you notice ear pain or ringing, lower the volume.

- Q: Can a volume booster damage my speaker or hearing?
  A: Very high volume can. Raise the level gradually, keep an eye on the Safe/Caution/Danger colors, and lower it if sound distorts or your ears hurt.
- Q: How much louder can it go?
  A: Up to 225% (+15 dB) with Pro, and up to 183% (+10 dB) on the free version, on top of your device volume. Actual loudness varies by device, headphones and content.

Page: https://codedac.com/guides/make-android-phone-louder.html

## How to hide personal info in screenshots and PDFs on Windows

Screenshots and scanned documents often contain a phone number, an email, a card or ID number, an address or a face. Before you send or post them from your PC, cover that information so it can't be recovered.

### Option 1: Snipping Tool

Recent versions of Snipping Tool on Windows 11 can hide email addresses and phone numbers in a screenshot through Text actions, and you can draw over anything else. Avoid the highlighter for this — it is semi-transparent — and use solid strokes that cover each item completely.

### Option 2: PhotoCleaner+ for Windows

PhotoCleaner+ for Windows (our app) finds likely personal info in photos, screenshots and PDFs — phone numbers, emails, card numbers, IBAN, passport numbers, names, addresses, license plates, faces and QR codes — and exports a copy with solid masks. Everything runs on your PC; nothing is uploaded.

1. Open a file, paste it with Ctrl+V, drag it onto the window, or right-click it in File Explorer and choose Clean with PhotoCleaner+.
2. Review the boxes: click to turn one on or off, drag to move or resize, and draw your own over anything that was missed.
3. Export the masked copy — save, copy, share, or save as PDF. Your original is never overwritten, and saved copies carry no metadata.

### Free and Pro

Finding personal info is free and unlimited, and you can export 3 documents a day for free. Pro is a one-time purchase that removes the daily limit and adds PDF export and printing. There are no ads and no watermark.

- Q: Will it find every piece of personal info?
  A: No tool can promise that. Detection is a starting point — always check the boxes before you export and draw over anything that was missed.
- Q: Are my files uploaded?
  A: No. Detection, masking and export run on your PC, with no account and nothing uploaded.

Page: https://codedac.com/guides/hide-personal-info-in-screenshots-windows.html

## How to keep a live crypto ticker on top of other windows on Windows

Keeping an exchange tab open means switching to it every time you want a price. A floating ticker keeps the coins you follow in view above every window.

### Set up FloatCrypto+ for Windows

FloatCrypto+ for Windows (our app) keeps a slim ticker on top of every window, showing each coin's symbol and 24-hour change. It never takes focus, so your cursor stays where you were typing.

1. Install FloatCrypto+ from the Microsoft Store; it lives in the system tray.
2. Pick coins from the Binance pairs and drag them into your order.
3. Place the ticker anywhere, and adjust its opacity and text size — or collapse it into a bubble at the screen edge.
4. Set a target above or below the current price to get a desktop notification when the market crosses it. Double-click a coin for its chart.

### Good to know

Hover the tray icon for a full price table, and hide the ticker with Ctrl+Alt+T. Prices come from Binance's public market data with automatic fallback and may be delayed by up to 30 seconds; the app doesn't trade or connect to an exchange account, and nothing in it is investment advice.

Free follows 2 coins with 1 alert; Pro is a one-time purchase for 10 coins, unlimited alerts, a 10-second refresh and longer charts. There are no ads.

- Q: Does the ticker get in the way of my work?
  A: No. It never takes focus; you can lower its opacity, collapse it into a bubble, or hide it with Ctrl+Alt+T.
- Q: Does it need my exchange account?
  A: No. It reads public market data only and never trades or holds funds.
